summary: 7 Nights on Mars turns the challenges of space exploration into a story players help shape: a stranded crew, a damaged habitat, and seven nights to find a way home. We developed a 2D game that addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by asking players to weigh competing priorities and live with the consequences of their decisions. With limited resources and no perfect solution, every choice involves deciding what the mission can afford and what it cannot afford to lose. Inspired by NASA research, the experience introduces students to the interconnected nature of mission planning and operations. Its purpose is to spark curiosity about space science while encouraging critical thinking, adaptability, and an understanding of the human responsibility behind engineering decisions.
details:
7 Nights on Mars is a 2D survival and mission management game that puts players in charge of a damaged Martian habitat. With seven nights to keep the crew alive and prepare for departure, players must decide how to spend limited time, power, water, and oxygen. Our response to the Space Mission Design Game challenge focuses on mission operations: turning engineering trade-offs into decisions players can experience and learn from.

The game connects four stations: a greenhouse, a life-support system inspired by MOXIE, a biomedical terminal, and a communications antenna. Each decision affects the wider mission. Growing food requires water, lighting, and heating, while producing oxygen competes for the same limited battery power. Communicating with Earth means choosing which information matters most, and caring for the crew becomes just as important as maintaining equipment. At dawn, players see the consequences of their choices and adapt their strategy for the next night. Eight possible endings and a final mission report encourage experimentation.

We built the game in Unity using C#, with GitHub for collaboration and version control. Its creative approach combines pixel art, storytelling, and interconnected resource management to make space exploration approachable for students. NASA resources informed the scientific concepts, while simplified rules keep the experience understandable and playable. Throughout development, we considered clarity, difficulty, scientific grounding, and how to make failure useful for learning. Our goal is to help players understand why a successful mission depends on balancing the needs of an entire system.
